strategies.name: Detection Strategy for Forged Web Credentials

analytics.name: Analytic 0717
analytics.guidance: Defenders may detect adversaries forging web credentials in IaaS environments by monitoring for anomalous API activity such as AssumeRole or GetFederationToken being executed by unusual principals. These events often correlate with sudden logon sessions from unfamiliar IP addresses or regions. The chain is usually secret material misuse (stolen private key or password) → API request generating a new token → access to high-value resources.

tuning.description: Define expected users and roles allowed to use AssumeRole or federation APIs.
Alert if the same user authenticates from geographically disparate locations within a short time.

log_sources.name: AWS:CloudTrail
log_sources.channel: AssumeRole, GetFederationToken API calls by unusual or new entities

log_sources.name: AWS:CloudTrail
log_sources.channel: Temporary security credentials used to authenticate into management console or APIs

analytics.name: Analytic 0718
analytics.guidance: Forged web credentials may manifest as anomalous SAML token issuance, OpenID Connect token minting, or Zimbra pre-auth key usage. Defenders may see tokens issued without normal authentication events, multiple valid tokens generated simultaneously, or signing anomalies in IdP logs.

tuning.description: Limit the maximum time temporary tokens are valid.
Define normal authentication flows (e.g., password+MFA) to baseline token issuance.

log_sources.name: azure:signinlogs
log_sources.channel: SAML/OIDC tokens issued without corresponding MFA or password validation

log_sources.name: NSM:Connections
log_sources.channel: Pre-authentication keys generated or token signing anomalies

analytics.name: Analytic 0719
analytics.guidance: Forged web credentials on Windows endpoints may be detected by anomalous browser cookie files, local token cache manipulations, or tools injecting tokens into sessions. Defenders may observe processes accessing LSASS or browser credential stores unexpectedly, followed by unusual logon sessions.

tuning.description: Define expected processes that access LSASS or browser credential files.

analytics.name: Analytic 0720
analytics.guidance: On Linux systems, forged credentials may be injected into browser session files, curl/wget headers, or token caches in memory. Detection can leverage auditd to track processes accessing sensitive files (~/.mozilla, ~/.config/chromium, ~/.aws/credentials) and correlate with suspicious outbound connections.

tuning.description: Define which credential and session files should trigger monitoring.

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: Processes reading credential or token cache files

log_sources.name: WinEventLog:Sysmon
log_sources.channel: Outbound requests with forged tokens/cookies in headers

analytics.name: Analytic 0721
analytics.guidance: Forged credentials on macOS may be visible through Unified Logs showing abnormal access to Keychain or browser session files. Correlated with anomalous web session usage from Safari or Chrome processes outside typical user context.

tuning.description: List applications that normally request Keychain credentials.

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Access to Keychain items or browser credential stores

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Web sessions initiated with newly forged tokens

analytics.name: Analytic 0722
analytics.guidance: SaaS platforms may show forged credentials as unusual API keys, tokens, or session cookies being used without corresponding authentication. Correlated patterns include simultaneous valid sessions from multiple geographies, unusual API calls with new tokens, or bypass of expected MFA enforcement.

tuning.description: Trigger on logins from unusual or high-risk geographies.
Detect multiple simultaneous uses of the same forged credential.

log_sources.name: m365:unified
log_sources.channel: Session creation without MFA or login event

log_sources.name: saas:auth
log_sources.channel: API requests made with tokens not associated with expected user logins

analytics.name: Analytic 0723
analytics.guidance: Forged web credentials in Office Suite contexts may appear as abnormal authentication headers in Outlook or Teams traffic, or unexplained OAuth grants in M365/Azure logs. Defenders should correlate token usage events with missing authentication flows and mismatched device/user context.

tuning.description: Approved OAuth apps and flows; flag unapproved or unexpected token grants.

log_sources.name: m365:oauth
log_sources.channel: OAuth grants or tokens issued without expected user consent

log_sources.name: m365:signinlogs
log_sources.channel: Token usage events with device/user mismatch
